finding_type: LIMITATION of the harness (not a bug)
title: Break-case detection is calibrated at the single most favorable layer; the drop from layer 0 is a step, not a depth gradient
note: Supersedes this artifact's own prior version, which compared only layer 0 against layer 13 and inferred a monotonic-depth-decay mechanism from those two points. That mechanism is now refuted by a five-point sweep. This version records the sweep, both refuted mechanism hypotheses, a third candidate marked explicitly as unconfirmed inference, and the sharper consequence for the gate.

SWEEP: --layer in {0, 7, 13, 20, 27} (28 layers total, 0-indexed, so 27 is the last), all five runs at --tp 2 --repetitions 20 --batch 2 --seq-len 8 (the exact configuration tolerance/phase2a_bf16_floor_v2.json's reproduction used). Floor mean_deviation is IDENTICAL across all five runs (3.898e-02) as expected -- the floor has no injection and cannot depend on where a break case would target; the whole effect below is confined to the break-case legs.

DATA (mean_deviation per case, threshold 5.847e-01 = 15 * 3.898e-02): layer 0 -- case1 1.772, case2 1.570, case3 2.984, verdict PASS (weakest case2 clears threshold by 2.685x). layer 7 -- case1 0.2766, case2 0.2265, case3 0.2675, verdict FAIL. layer 13 -- case1 0.2269, case2 0.1617, case3 0.4996, verdict FAIL. layer 20 -- case1 0.4449, case2 0.2092, case3 1.052, verdict FAIL (case3 alone would individually clear the threshold at this layer -- 1.052 > 0.5847 -- but the gate verdict is per-configuration, gated on the WEAKEST case, which is case2 at every layer tested). layer 27 -- case1 0.5227, case2 0.2150, case3 0.4448, verdict FAIL.

BOTH PRIOR MECHANISM HYPOTHESES ARE REFUTED BY THIS SWEEP. (1) The distribution-specific hypothesis (case 3 tracks that layer's own norm-weight distribution while cases 1/2 hold steady) was already refuted by the two-point layer-0-vs-13 comparison (all three cases moved by a similar factor there) and remains refuted here. (2) The monotonic-depth-decay hypothesis floated after that same two-point comparison (break magnitude decreases steadily with distance from the logits, ~0.85x per layer) is ALSO refuted by this sweep: it predicted a smooth decrease from layer 0 through 27, with layer 27 the SMALLEST. Neither holds. Layer 0 sits 2.8x-11.2x above the corresponding case at every other tested layer (per-case ratios: case1 3.4x-7.8x, case2 6.9x-9.7x, case3 2.8x-11.2x, computed layer0-value / layerN-value across N in {7,13,20,27}). Layers 7 through 27, in contrast, form a band with mild NON-monotonic structure: case1 rises gently from layer 7 (0.2766) to layer 27 (0.5227); case2 is close to flat (0.2265 to 0.2150, no clear trend); case3 peaks at layer 20 (1.052) rather than decreasing monotonically toward 27 (0.4448 there, lower than at layer 0's neighbor 7 at 0.2675 -- not monotonic in either direction).

A THIRD CANDIDATE, MARKED EXPLICITLY AS AN UNCONFIRMED INFERENCE -- not a traced mechanism, and offered after two prior mechanism guesses from this same investigation were both wrong: layer 0 is the only layer whose input is the raw token embedding rather than a residual stream that already carries accumulated contributions from every preceding block. A perturbation injected there acts on a signal with nothing else yet mixed in, and is then carried through and amplified across all 27 subsequent blocks with no prior dilution; a perturbation injected at any other layer is added into a stream that already carries most of the eventual representation, competing with everything already accumulated. This candidate predicts exactly the shape the data shows -- a STEP between layer 0 and every other layer, not a gradient across layers 7-27 -- where the refuted monotonic-decay hypothesis predicted a gradient across ALL layers including 0. It has not been confirmed by any residual-stream instrumentation; it is offered because it fits the observed step shape, not because it has been traced.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE, SHARPER THAN THE PRIOR (TWO-POINT) VERSION OF THIS FINDING: calibration at layer 0 is calibration at the single most favorable position in the model, and because the drop is a STEP rather than a GRADIENT, it cannot be corrected by a depth-dependent threshold (i.e. there is no way to scale SAFETY_FACTOR/GATE_MARGIN smoothly by distance-from-logits and have it track this data -- layers 7 through 27 fail by roughly similar amounts regardless of depth, so a depth-indexed correction would either still fail the non-zero layers or over-correct layer 0). Every one of the four non-zero layers tested fails the gate on its weakest case (case2 in all four); layer 0 is the only layer, of the five tested, where this gate's current constants would catch an injected bug of this shape and magnitude.

WHAT WOULD DISCRIMINATE FURTHER, NOT YET RUN: this sweep already answers the immediate question (is layer 0 representative -- no) and identifies the step as being specifically between layer 0 and layer 7, but does not test layers 1-6, so the step's exact location (is it a hard boundary right after layer 0, or a fast-but-continuous drop across the first few layers) is unresolved. A finer sweep over {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7} would locate it. Separately, the embedding-input candidate above could be tested directly (not merely inferred) by instrumenting residual-stream norms at each block boundary during a forward pass and checking whether the perturbation's relative contribution to the stream drops sharply after layer 0 specifically, rather than gradually -- this needs the box and has not been attempted.

results.note: case3 alone (1.052) individually clears the threshold at this layer; the gate verdict is still FAIL because it gates on the weakest case, case2.

refuted_hypotheses: H1 (distribution-specific, from the break-case-ordering-inversion investigation): case 3 tracks that layer's own norm-weight distribution while cases 1/2 hold steady. Refuted by the original layer-0-vs-13 comparison (all three cases moved by a similar factor) and remains refuted here.

H2 (monotonic depth decay, floated after H1's refutation): break magnitude decreases steadily with distance from the logits across all 28 layers, ~0.85x per layer. Refuted by this sweep: layer 27 is not the smallest value for any case, and layers 7-27 show mild non-monotonic structure (case1 rises 7->27, case2 is flat, case3 peaks at 20) rather than a steady decrease.
candidate_mechanism_unconfirmed: Layer 0 is uniquely the raw-token-embedding input, not an already-accumulated residual stream; a perturbation there is carried through and amplified across all 27 subsequent blocks with no prior dilution, while a perturbation at any other layer competes with a stream that already carries most of the eventual representation. Predicts a STEP between layer 0 and the rest, matching the observed shape, where H2 predicted a gradient across all layers including 0. Explicitly marked as inference from the observed shape, not a traced mechanism -- offered after two prior mechanism guesses in this same investigation (the distribution-specific one and the monotonic-decay one) were both wrong.
consequence: Calibration at layer 0 is calibration at the single most favorable position in the model. Because the drop is a step (layer 0 vs. everything else) rather than a gradient across layers, it cannot be corrected by a depth-dependent threshold -- there is no smooth depth-indexed scaling of SAFETY_FACTOR/GATE_MARGIN that tracks this data. Every one of the four non-zero layers tested fails the gate on its weakest case (case2 in all four); layer 0 is the only layer, of the five tested, where the current gate would catch an injected bug of this shape and magnitude.
next_test_not_run: Finer sweep over layers {1,2,3,4,5,6} to locate the step precisely (hard boundary right after layer 0, vs. a fast-but-continuous drop over the first few layers). Separately, direct residual-stream-norm instrumentation during a forward pass to test the embedding-input candidate mechanism rather than merely infer it from the outcome shape.
